analyzed_vuln.description: SkTriangulateSimplePolygon classifies near-collinear vertices as reflex and inserts them into ReflexHash. ReflexHash::hash computes grid coordinates from vertex positions and bounds, but does not validate/clamp the computed (h,v) indices before returning v*fHCount+h. For malformed/fuzzed polygons, hash can become negative or out of range, so ReflexHash::add uses an invalid fGrid[index] element and then SkTInternalLList::addToTail dereferences corrupted memory, causing the SEGV.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In api_polyutils, attacker-controlled input sets polygon vertex count/coordinates and indexMap. When count>=3 and bounds/winding checks pass, SkTriangulateSimplePolygon initializes ReflexHash and adds reflex vertices. If vertex geometry (e.g., degenerate/near-collinear or numerically unstable coordinates relative to bounds/grid conversion) makes ReflexHash::hash produce an out-of-bounds index, fGrid[index].addToTail is called on invalid memory. Debug-only SkASSERT in hash is not enforced in fuzz/release, so crafted polygon data can trigger the crash.
